people.VITELLOZZO: Condottiere of the Vitelli dynasty. Their life was connected with Florence, Papal States.
people.BARTALVIANO: Condottiere of the Alviano dynasty. Their life was connected with Papal States.
people.PAPA_INOCENCIO3: One of the most powerful popes of the Middle Ages. He was active in European politics, convened the IV Lateran Council and exercised strong tutelage over kings and crusaders.
people.PAPA_HONORIO3: Cencio Savelli, a Camarlian of the Church and tutor of the young Frederick II, was pope between 1216 and 1227. He approved the Dominican order (1216) and Franciscan rule (1223), and crowned Emperor Frederick II in 1220.
people.PAPA_GREGORIO9: Pope with strong legal and political personality, great adversary of Frederick II. His pontificate reinforced the papal Inquisition and deepened the conflict between the papacy and the Empire.
people.PAPA_CELESTINO4: Goffredo da Castiglione was elected in 1241 in a conclave closed by Senator Matteo Rosso Orsini and died seventeen days later. After his death, the seat was vacant for almost two years.
people.PAPA_INOCENCIO4: Pope confronted Frederick II in the final phase of the great conflict between papacy and Empire. The Council of Lyon of 1245 declared the emperor deposed and radicalised the political struggle.
people.PAPA_ALEJANDRO4: Rinaldo dei Conti di Segni, nephew of Gregory IX, was pope between 1254 and 1261. He continued the struggle against the Hohenstaufen in the kingdom of Sicily and canonized St. Clare of Assisi in 1255.
people.PAPA_URBANO4: Jacques Pantaléon, son of a Troyes shoemaker and former Latin patriarch of Jerusalem, was pope between 1261 and 1264. He instituted the feast of Corpus Christi and offered the kingdom of Sicily to Charles of Anjou in front of Manfredo.
people.PAPA_CLEMENTE4: Guy Foulques, a Provencal jurist and adviser to Louis IX, became a clergyman when he was widowed and was pope between 1265 and 1268. He invested the kingdom of Sicily to Charles of Anjou, who defeated Manfredo at Benevento (1266) and Conradino at Tagliacozzo (1268).
people.PAPA_INOCENCIO5: Pierre de Tarentaise, Dominican theologian and archbishop of Lyon, was the first pope of the order of preachers. He ruled the Church for only a few months in 1276.
people.PAPA_ADRIANO5: Ottobuono Fieschi, nephew of Innocent IV and legate in England during the Barons' War, was elected in 1276 and died a little over a month later, having not received priestly ordination.
people.PAPA_JUAN21: Portuguese physician and philosopher, traditionally identified with Pedro Hispano, author of the Summulae logicales, was pope from 1276. He died in 1277 when the roof of his stay in Viterbo's palace collapsed.
people.PAPA_NICOLAS3: Giovanni Gaetano Orsini, of the great Roman family, was pope between 1277 and 1280. He obtained from Rudolf of Habsburg the renunciation of the Roman Empire and favored his relatives, so Dante places him among the Simonics.
people.PAPA_MARTIN4: Simon de Brion, French and former chancellor of Louis IX, was pope between 1281 and 1285. He supported Charles of Anjou after the Sicilian Vespers (1282), excommunicated Peter III of Aragon and offered his kingdom to Charles of Valois, son of the king of France.
people.PAPA_HONORIO4: Giacomo Savelli, nephew of Honorius III, was pope between 1285 and 1287. He continued to support the Angevinists against the Crown of Aragon in the war for Sicily.
people.PAPA_NICOLAS4: Girolamo Masci, former general of the Franciscans, was the first pope of that order (1288–1292). He pushed missions into Asia and saw Acre, the last bastion crossed in the Holy Land, fall in 1291.
people.PAPA_CELESTINO5: Pietro da Morrone, an Abruzzo hermit, was elected pope in 1294 after more than two years of vacant office. He gave up at five months, and his successor Boniface VIII kept him in custody until his death in 1296.
people.PAPA_BONIFACIO8: Pope of strong theocratic conception, facing Philip IV of France head on. His pontificate culminated in the Anagni crisis, a symbol of the retreat of the papal political power against the monarchies.
people.PAPA_BENEDICTO11: Niccolò Boccasini, the general master of the Dominicans, was elected in 1303, after the death of Boniface VIII. He lifted some of the convictions against Philip IV of France and died in Perugia after eight months of pontificate.
people.PAPA_CLEMENTE5: French Pope whose pontificate was linked to the transfer of the pontifical court to Avignon and the suppression of the Order of the Temple under the pressure of Philip IV of France.
people.PAPA_JUAN22: Pope of Avignon whose long pontificate was marked by conflicts with Louis IV of Bavaria and by a strong financial and administrative reorganization of the curia.
people.PAPA_BENEDICTO12: Jacques Fournier, Cistercian and inquisitor at Pamiers, was pope at Avignon between 1334 and 1342. He began the construction of the palace of the Popes and reformed the religious orders.
people.PAPA_CLEMENTE6: Pierre Roger, Benedictine and chancellor of Philip VI of France, was pope at Avignon between 1342 and 1352. He bought the city from Queen Joanna of Naples in 1348 and expanded the palace with a lavish court.
people.PAPA_INOCENCIO6: Étienne Aubert, a lemosine jurist, was pope at Avignon between 1352 and 1362. He sent Cardinal Gil de Albornoz to recover for the Holy See the government of the Pontifical States.
people.PAPA_URBANO5: William of Grimoard, Benedictine and canonist, was pope between 1362 and 1370. He returned to Rome in 1367, but returned to Avignon in 1370 and died there that same year.
people.PAPA_GREGORIO11: Pierre Roger de Beaufort, nephew of Clement VI, was the last pope of Avignon. He moved the court to Rome in 1377, and his death, the following year, preceded the schism of the West.
people.PAPA_URBANO6: Bartholomew Prignan, archbishop of Bari, was elected in Rome in 1378. His harshness led the cardinals to elect Clement VII, and so began the schism of the West.
people.PAPA_BONIFACIO9: Pietro Tomacelli, a Neapolitan, was the pope of Roman obedience between 1389 and 1404, during the schism. He restored pontifical authority in Rome and the Church States.
people.PAPA_INOCENCIO7: Cosimo Migliorati was the pope of Roman obedience between 1404 and 1406. A revolt in Rome forced him to take refuge in Viterbo in 1405.
people.PAPA_GREGORIO12: Angelo Correr, Venetian, was the Roman pope of the Schism between 1406 and 1415. He resigned before the Council of Constance to allow the election of Martin V and the end of the schism.
people.PAPA_MARTIN5: Pope whose election at the Council of Constance put an end to the Great Schism of the West. His return to Rome began the political reconstruction of the Papal States.
people.PAPA_EUGENIO4: Gabriele Condulmer, a Venetian and nephew of Gregory XII, was pope between 1431 and 1447. He opposed the Council of Basel and presided at Florence (1439) over the ephemeral union with the Greek Church.
people.PAPA_NICOLAS5: Humanist Pope and patron saint who promoted the cultural renewal of Rome. His library and artistic projects prepared the great papal patronage of the Renaissance.
people.PAPA_PIO2: Pope humanist, diplomat and writer, formerly known as Eneas Silvio Piccolomini. He defended a renewed crusade against the Ottomans and left valuable autobiographical writings.
people.PAPA_PAULO2: Pietro Barbo, Venetian and nephew of Eugene IV, was pope between 1464 and 1471. He built the palace of St. Mark, today Palazzo Venezia, and dissolved the Roman academy of Pomponio Leto.
people.PAPA_SIXTO4: A Renaissance pope who strengthened his family's power through nepotism and promoted great works in Rome. He gave the Sistine Chapel its name and was involved in Italian politics of his time.
people.PAPA_INOCENCIO8: Giovanni Battista Cibo, a Genoese, was pope between 1484 and 1492. He published the bull against the witchcraft Summis desiderantes (1484) and married his son Franceschetto to a daughter of Lorenzo de Medici.
people.PAPA_PIO3: Francesco Todeschini Piccolomini, nephew of Pius II, was elected in September 1503 and died twenty-six days later.
people.PAPA_JULIO2: The Renaissance pope, political commander and great patron. He pushed the reconstruction of St. Peter's and commissioned decisive works to Michelangelo, Raphael and Bramante while fighting to strengthen the Pontifical States.
people.PAPA_LEON10: Pope Medici and the great patrons of the Renaissance. His pontificate coincided with the beginning of Luther's Reformation and with an intense Italian and cultural politics.
people.PAPA_ADRIANO6: Hadrian of Utrecht, preceptor of Charles V and governor of Castile during the Communities, was pope between 1522 and 1523. He was the last non-Italian pope until 1978.
people.PAPA_CLEMENTE7: Pope Medici caught between Francis I and Charles V during the Italian wars. His pontificate was marked by the plunder of Rome in 1527 and by the marital crisis of Henry VIII.
people.PAPA_PAULO3: Pope Farnesius who promoted Catholic renewal and called the Council of Trent. His pontificate was decisive in the institutionalization of the Counter-Reformation.
people.PAPA_JULIO3: Giovanni Maria Ciocchi del Monte, one of the presidents of the Council of Trent, was pope between 1550 and 1555. He reopened the council in 1551 and built the villa Giulia in Rome.
people.PAPA_MARCELO2: Marcello Cervini, humanist and president of the Council of Trent, was pope for twenty-two days in 1555. Palestrina dedicated the Mass of the Papae Marcelli to him.
people.PAPA_PAULO4: Gian Pietro Carafa, co-founder of the Teatinos and reorganizer of the Roman Inquisition, was pope between 1555 and 1559. He created the ghetto of Rome, enacted the first Index of Forbidden Books and confronted Philip II.
people.PAPA_PIO4: Giovanni Angelo Medici, Milanese unrelated to the Medici of Florence, was pope between 1559 and 1565. He reopened and concluded the Council of Trent (1562~1563); his nephew Carlos Borromeo led his government.
people.PAPA_PIO5: Pope Dominic and central figure of the Catholic Reformation. He promoted the application of Trent and the Holy League which defeated the Ottoman fleet at Lepanto in 1571.
people.PAPA_GREGORIO13: Pope known for the reform of the calendar that bears his name. He also promoted Catholic education and the strengthening of Counter-Reformation institutions.
people.PAPA_SIXTO5: Pope of brief but energetic pontificate, he reorganized the administration of the curia and transformed Rome urbanistically through great works and new monumental paths.
people.PAPA_URBANO7: Giovanni Battista Castagna was pope for thirteen days in 1590 and died of malaria before his coronation.
people.PAPA_GREGORIO14: Niccolò Sfondrati, bishop of Cremona, was pope from 1590 to 1591. He supported the Catholic League against Henry of Navarre in France's wars of religion.
people.PAPA_INOCENCIO9: Giovanni Antonio Facchinetti, Bolognese, was pope for two months in 1591.
people.PAPA_CLEMENTE8: Ippolito Aldobrandini was pope between 1592 and 1605. He absolved Henry IV of France (1595), incorporated Ferrara into the Church States (1598) and presided over the jubilee of 1600.
people.PAPA_LEON11: Alessandro de' Medici, of the Florentine family, was elected in April 1605 and died twenty-seven days later.
people.PAPA_PAULO5: Camillo Borghese was pope from 1605 to 1621. He launched the Endeavour against Venice (1606) and finished the facade of St. Peter; his nephew Scipione Borghese assembled a large art collection.
people.PAPA_GREGORIO15: Alessandro Ludovisi, a Bolognese, was pope from 1621 to 1623. He created the Congregation of Propaganda Fide (1622), regulated the conclave by secret ballot and canonized Ignatius of Loyola and Francisco Javier.
people.PAPA_URBANO8: Pope Barberini during the Thirty Years' War. His pontificate combined great artistic patronage, family politics and the famous trial against Galileo.
people.PAPA_INOCENCIO10: Giovanni Battista Pamphilj was pope from 1644 to 1655. He protested the peace of Westphalia and commissioned Bernini to source the Four Rivers; Velázquez painted his portrait in 1650.
people.PAPA_ALEJANDRO7: Fabio Chigi, Sienese and nuncio to Münster during the negotiations of Westphalia, was pope between 1655 and 1667. He commissioned Bernini to write the column in St. Peter's Square and received Christina of Sweden in Rome.
people.PAPA_CLEMENTE9: Giulio Rospigliosi, librettist and diplomat, was pope between 1667 and 1669. He mediated the peace of Aachen (1668) and supported Venice in the defense of Candia.
people.PAPA_CLEMENTE10: Emilio Altieri was elected in 1670, at almost eighty years of age, and his adopted nephew, Cardinal Paluzzo Altieri, led the government until his death in 1676.
people.PAPA_INOCENCIO11: Pope reformer and opponent of the ecclesiastical policy of Louis XIV. He supported the European resistance to the Ottoman advance of the late 17th century.
people.PAPA_ALEJANDRO8: Pietro Ottoboni, Venetian, was pope between 1689 and 1691. He helped Venice in the war against the Ottomans and condemned the Gallic Declaration of 1682.
people.CARD_FRANCESCO_PIGN: Cardinal theatrical and archbishop of Naples. He was related to Innocent XII by a branch other than the Pignatelli, not a direct nephew of the pope.
people.PAPA_INOCENCIO12: Antonio Pignatelli, of the Cerchiara branch, was pope as Innocent XII. His parents were Francesco Pignatelli of Spinazzola and Porzia Carafa; the pontifical career should not be confused with the Neapolitan family lordships.
people.PAPA_CLEMENTE11: Giovanni Francesco Albani was pope from 1700 to 1721. In the War of Spanish Succession he had to recognize Arch Duke Charles as king of Spain (1709), and he condemned Jansenism with the Bull Unigenitus (1713).
people.PAPA_INOCENCIO13: Michelangelo Conti, of the same family as Innocent III, was pope between 1721 and 1724.
people.PAPA_BENEDICTO13: Pietro Francesco Orsini, Dominican and Archbishop of Benevento, was pope from 1724 to 1730. He left the government in the hands of his secretary, Cardinal Niccolò Coscia.
people.PAPA_CLEMENTE12: Lorenzo Corsini, Florentine, was pope between 1730 and 1740. Blind since 1732, he condemned Freemasonry in 1738 and undertook the construction of the Trevi fountain.
people.PAPA_BENEDICTO14: Prospero Lambertini, a Bolognese canonist, was pope from 1740 to 1758. He signed concordates with Spain and other states and kept correspondence with scholars of the Enlightenment.
people.PAPA_CLEMENTE13: Carlo Rezzonico, Venetian, was pope from 1758 to 1769. He defended the Society of Jesus against its expulsion from Portugal, France, Spain and Naples.
people.PAPA_CLEMENTE14: Lorenzo Ganganelli, a Franciscan convent, was pope from 1769 to 1774. Pressured by the Bourbons, he suppressed the Society of Jesus in 1773.
people.PAPA_PIO6: Pope between 1775 and 1799. He faced the ecclesiastical reforms of Joseph II and the French Revolution; French troops occupied Rome and died a prisoner in Valence.
people.IGNACIOLOYOLA: Iñigo López de Loyola, born into a family of the small Basque nobility, changed his life after being wounded in the defense of Pamplona in 1521. His spiritual experience gave rise to the Exercises. In Paris he gathered the companions of the future Society of Jesus, approved by Paul III in 1540, of which he was first superior general.

people.GIOVANNAMONTEFELTRO: Consort of the Montefeltro dynasty. Her life was connected with Papal States.
people.FRANCESCOROVEREURBINO: Duke of Urbino, 1508 to 1516. Duke of Urbino of the Della Rovere dynasty.
people.PIETROALDOBRANDINI_CARD: Cardinal of the Aldobrandini dynasty. Their life was connected with Papal States.
people.SCIPIONEBORGHESE: Cardinal of the Borghese dynasty. Their life was connected with Papal States.
people.FRANCESCOBARBERINI: Nephew of Urban VIII and brother of Taddeus and Anthony, Francesco Barberini was created cardinal in 1623. He performed diplomatic and governmental functions and assembled an important library of manuscripts. After the election of Innocent X, he took refuge in France in 1646; he later returned to Rome, where he died in 1679.
people.ANTONIOBARBERINI: The son of Carlo Barberini and Costanza Magalotti, he was one of the nephews of Urban VIII: his appointment, reserved since 1627, was made public in 1628. He shared with his brothers Francesco and Taddeo the power and patronage of the family and, after 1644, the difficulties with Innocent X. He's different from his uncle, the Capuchin cardinal of the same name.
people.FLAVIOCHIGI_CARD: Cardinal of the Chigi dynasty. Their life was connected with Papal States.
people.OLIMPIAMANCINI: Nephew of Cardinal Mazarino, prominent figure at the court of Louis XIV and wife of Eugenio Mauricio de Savoy, Count of Soissons. Involved in the "affair of poisons", she fled France in 1680 and lived in the Spanish Netherlands; she was the mother of Prince Eugene.
people.IPPOLITOMEDICI: Cardinal of the Médici dynasty. Their life was connected with Florence, Papal States.
people.ASCANIOCOLONNA: Duke of the Colonna dynasty. His life was connected with Naples, Papal States.
people.GIOVANNAARAGCOL: Noble of the Trastámara-Nápoles dynasty. Her life was connected with Naples, Papal States.
people.MARCANTONIO2COL: Roman nobleman and admiral in the service of the Spanish Monarchy and the papacy. He commanded one of the great wings of the Holy League fleet at the Battle of Lepanto.
people.PAPA_PIO7: Barnaba Chiaramonti, a Benedictine born in Cesena in 1742, was elected in Venice in 1800. He signed the Concordat with Napoleon (1801), attended his coronation (1804) and was his prisoner between 1809 and 1814; he died in 1823.
people.MAZARINO: Italian-born diplomat, cardinal and chief minister during the reign of Anna of Austria and the youth of Louis XIV. He overcame the Fronde and intervened in the negotiations of Westphalia and the peace of the Pyrenees.

name: Crown of Castile
summary: The Crown of Castile designates a political body, not a kingdom that eliminates its components. Its consolidation from 1230 brought together under one monarch Castile and Leon and the territories incorporated into its expansion.

uniones.resumen: Ferdinand III gathered two heritages. The continuity of a common monarch did not immediately erase the legal identities and traditions of the kingdoms.
uniones.instituciones: The Crown of Castile was a composite structure in evolution. Castile, Leon and Spain are not three equivalent or interchangeable kingdoms in the filters.

uniones.resumen: Isabel and Fernando linked their crowns through marriage and shared government. Their heirs accumulated rights of different origins.
uniones.instituciones: The crowns retained their own institutions, taxation and laws. Isabel's death in 1504 separated her successive trajectories before Charles's accession; the decrees of Nueva Planta later transformed that organization.

personas.resumen: King of Aragon and, along with Isabel I, protagonist of the dynastic union of the Spanish crowns. His policy combined peninsular consolidation, Mediterranean expansion and intense marital diplomacy.

Queen of Castile and one of the central figures in the formation of the Spanish Monarchy. She ruled alongside Fernando de Aragón and presided over a decisive stage of political and territorial expansion.

personas.resumen: Emperor of the Holy Empire and sovereign of a composite monarchy that extended to the Iberian Peninsula, Italy, the Netherlands and America. From Philip I he inherited the Franco County, Artois, Namur and Luxembourg, as well as other Dutch territories. It later incorporated Frisia, Utrecht, Overijssel, Drente, Groningen and Güeldres in a phased manner, between 1524 and 1543. He retained the ducal dignity of Burgundy, but did not rule the duchy incorporated into France. From 1535 he kept Milan under imperial control; the investiture and subsequent possession of Philip II must be distinguished from that government.

eventos.titulo: Marriage of Isabella of Castile and Fernando of Aragon

Charles V demands that Luther withdraw. The refusal of the reformer and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transformed a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected King of the Romans

Philip Melanchthon presents before Charles V a systematic exhibition of the Lutheran faith, supported by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeated the League of Esmalkalde and captured its two great leaders, but the military victory failed to restore the religious unity of the Empire.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Henry of Navarre a presumed heir. Henry of Guisa reorganizes the Catholic League, backed by Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.
Louis XII and Ferdinand the Catholic agree to divide the kingdom of Frederick I. Cooperation is short-lived: disputes over the boundaries of partition turn former allies into enemies.

eventos.titulo: Cerignola: The Great Captain Changes the War
eventos.descripcion: Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba's forces defeated the French at Cerignola. The combined use of infantry, field fortifications and firearms consolidated Aragonese position in southern Italy.
A second major victory for the Grand Captain forces the French forces to retreat. The balance born of the 1500 cast is definitely broken in Fernando's favor.

eventos.titulo: Fernando brings together Naples and Trinacria under his crown
eventos.descripcion: The French defeat leaves Ferdinand the Catholic as king of Naples besides Trinacria. The two parts of the former Sicilian monarchy once again share sovereignty, although they will continue to be administered as separate kingdoms.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V achieves an agreement between the Spanish Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States. Philip II contributes an essential part of the resources and his half-brother Don John of Austria receives the supreme command of the Allied fleet.

name: Zeeland
summary: Zealand is registered as its own county, linked for long periods to the Netherlands. This matching of titles does not allow the use of Netherlands» as the name of the whole Dutch space or the deletion of particular rights over Zealand. The loaded succession is concentrated in the houses of Holland, Avesnes, Wittelsbach and Burgundy. The Jacqueline of Bavaria dispute affected this county along with Holland and Henao. The tabs show the terms of each title separately, even when the dates coincide.
notes: A county linked to the Netherlands, with its own succession and territorial identity; different from the grouping of the Netherlands.

eventos.descripcion: The marriage links the Burgundian heritage with the Habsburgs and changes the political balance of Western Europe.
The agreement returned Artois and the Frankish County to the heritage of Mary of Burgundy, while the duchy of Burgundy remained in French hands.
Charles V demands that Luther withdraw. The refusal of the reformer and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transformed a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
Imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Mutinous imperial troops plunder Rome during the Italian Wars.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by simple imperial imposition.
Charles V progressively divided his dominions between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgs.
Philip II's naval expedition against England failed after fighting, logistical problems and adverse weather.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected King of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I makes the imperial election a European competition. Charles brings together the imperial crown with a dynastic heritage that stretches from the Netherlands to Spain and America.
Philip Melanchthon presents before Charles V a systematic exhibition of the Lutheran faith, supported by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeated the League of Esmalkalde and captured its two great leaders, but the military victory failed to restore the religious unity of the Empire.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Henry of Navarre a presumed heir. Henry of Guisa reorganizes the Catholic League, backed by Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V achieves an agreement between the Spanish Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States. Philip II contributes an essential part of the resources and his half-brother Don John of Austria receives the supreme command of the Allied fleet.

name: Austria
summary: The duchy of Austria, centered on lands above and below the Enns, passed to the Habsburgs in 1282. The dignity of archduch, promoted in the 14th century and recognized in 1453, elevated the rank of title: it did not automatically convert Styria, Carinthia, Carniola or Tyrol into parts of the archduchy. Family branches ruled those lands separately over several periods.

eventos.titulo: Mary of Burgundy is married to Maximilian
eventos.descripcion: The marriage links the Burgundian heritage with the Habsburgs and changes the political balance of Western Europe.
The agreement returned Artois and the Frankish County to the heritage of Mary of Burgundy, while the duchy of Burgundy remained in French hands.
Charles V demands that Luther withdraw. The refusal of the reformer and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transformed a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
Imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Mutinous imperial troops plunder Rome during the Italian Wars.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by simple imperial imposition.
Charles V progressively divided his dominions between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgs.

eventos.titulo: Rudolf of Habsburg is elected king of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The election of Rudolf I closed the Great Interregnum and put the Habsburgs at the centre of imperial politics for the first time.

eventos.titulo: Marchfeld and the Austrian Habsburg base
eventos.descripcion: The defeat and death of Otakar II allowed the Habsburg appropriation of Austria and Styria, the territorial base of a dynasty that would still take generations to monopolize the imperial crown, to be consolidated.

eventos.titulo: Frederick III, Emperor of the Habsburgs
eventos.descripcion: The coronation of Frederick III inaugurated an extraordinary dynastic continuity: except for a brief interruption in the 18th century, imperial dignity would remain tied to the Habsburgs and then to the Habsburg-Lorraine.
The Worms Diet promotes common mechanisms of justice, public peace and political organization that seek to make a governmentable empire made up of hundreds of territorial powers.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected King of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I makes the imperial election a European competition. Charles brings together the imperial crown with a dynastic heritage that stretches from the Netherlands to Spain and America.
In the absence of a male heir, Charles VI attempts to secure the indivisibility of the Habsburg dominions and the succession of his future daughter Maria Teresa.

eventos.titulo: Charles VII breaks the Habsburg continuity
eventos.descripcion: In the midst of the War of Austrian Succession, the elector Wittelsbach Carlos Alberto obtains the imperial crown and proves that dignity remains elective, even after centuries of Habsburg predominance.

eventos.titulo: Francis I inaugurated the House of Habsburg-Lorraine
eventos.descripcion: The election of Francis Esteban returns the crown to the dynastic environment of Maria Theresa and creates the Habsburg-Lorraine line.
Joseph II succeeded his father as emperor and, after 1780, attempted to reform the Habsburg dominions quickly, clashing repeatedly with territorial and corporate privileges.
The French revolution upset the European political balance and turned the fate of Maria Antonieta, sister of Joseph II and Leopold II, into an international dynastic problem.

eventos.titulo: Francis II in the face of revolutionary Europe
eventos.descripcion: Francis II inherits the imperial crown in the midst of a revolutionary war. By 1800, the old empire was still in existence, but it was facing a transformation that would culminate a few years later.
Philip Melanchthon presents before Charles V a systematic exhibition of the Lutheran faith, supported by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeated the League of Esmalkalde and captured its two great leaders, but the military victory failed to restore the religious unity of the Empire.

The relief army led by John III Sobieski, with Polish, Habsburg and Holy Empire forces, broke through the Ottoman siege of Vienna on September 12, 1683. The victory opens a new phase of the war in Hungary and reinforces the rise of the Habsburg monarchy in Central Europe.

eventos.titulo: Hungarian rebellion opens a door to the sultan
eventos.descripcion: Imre Thököly leads a Hungarian opposition to the Habsburgs and seeks Ottoman support. The internal conflict of the monarchy of Leopold I is mixed with imperial rivalry in central Europe.

eventos.titulo: Leopold and Sobieski agree to help each other
eventos.descripcion: With papal mediation, Leopold I and John III Sobieski agree a defensive alliance. If Vienna or Krakow are attacked, the other sovereign must come to the aid of the ally.

The great vizier Kara Mustafa leads the Ottoman army to Vienna. Leopold leaves the capital and Ernst Rüdiger von Starhemberg organizes the defense as the fortifications suffer weeks of siege and mine work.

eventos.titulo: Poles, Emperors and German Princes gather
eventos.descripcion: Charles V of Lorraine coordinated the imperial forces and joined contingents from Bavaria, Saxony and other territories of the Empire. Sobieski arrives with the Polish army and takes command of the rescue operation.

eventos.titulo: From saving Vienna to moving on to the offensive
eventos.descripcion: After the victory, a new Holy League is formed. The Habsburgs, Poland and Venice transform an emergency defense into a prolonged war against the Ottoman Empire.
The conquest of Buddha shows that Vienna was not an isolated episode. The war that began in 1683 became a Habsburg expansion by Hungary and permanently altered the balance of central Europe.

name: Portugal
summary: Portugal consolidated its medieval territory with the conquest of the Algarve and developed an Atlantic expansion monarchy. The union with the Habsburgs was dynastic and it retained its own institutions until the restoration of Braganza.
notes: Portugal retained its own crown and institutions during the dynastic union of 1580-1640. Madeira has been represented since its settlement in 1425 and the whole of the Azores since 1452, when the western islands were also discovered.

uniones.resumen: Three Philippians shared the Portuguese and Spanish crowns after the succession crisis of 1580. The Portuguese Restoration of 1640 broke the common government.
uniones.instituciones: Portugal maintained its own laws, currency and administration. The effective separation of 1640 preceded the diplomatic recognition of 1668.

eventos.descripcion: The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by simple imperial imposition.

eventos.titulo: Rudolf of Habsburg is elected king of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The election of Rudolf I closed the Great Interregnum and put the Habsburgs at the centre of imperial politics for the first time.

eventos.titulo: Marchfeld and the Austrian Habsburg base
eventos.descripcion: The defeat and death of Otakar II allowed the Habsburg appropriation of Austria and Styria, the territorial base of a dynasty that would still take generations to monopolize the imperial crown, to be consolidated.
In the absence of a male heir, Charles VI attempts to secure the indivisibility of the Habsburg dominions and the succession of his future daughter Maria Teresa.

eventos.titulo: Charles VII breaks the Habsburg continuity
eventos.descripcion: In the midst of the War of Austrian Succession, the elector Wittelsbach Carlos Alberto obtains the imperial crown and proves that dignity remains elective, even after centuries of Habsburg predominance.

eventos.titulo: Francis I inaugurated the House of Habsburg-Lorraine
eventos.descripcion: The election of Francis Esteban returns the crown to the dynastic environment of Maria Theresa and creates the Habsburg-Lorraine line.
Joseph II succeeded his father as emperor and, after 1780, attempted to reform the Habsburg dominions quickly, clashing repeatedly with territorial and corporate privileges.
The French revolution upset the European political balance and turned the fate of Maria Antonieta, sister of Joseph II and Leopold II, into an international dynastic problem.

eventos.titulo: Francis II in the face of revolutionary Europe
eventos.descripcion: Francis II inherits the imperial crown in the midst of a revolutionary war. By 1800, the old empire was still in existence, but it was facing a transformation that would culminate a few years later.

The relief army led by John III Sobieski, with Polish, Habsburg and Holy Empire forces, broke through the Ottoman siege of Vienna on September 12, 1683. The victory opens a new phase of the war in Hungary and reinforces the rise of the Habsburg monarchy in Central Europe.

eventos.titulo: Hungarian rebellion opens a door to the sultan
eventos.descripcion: Imre Thököly leads a Hungarian opposition to the Habsburgs and seeks Ottoman support. The internal conflict of the monarchy of Leopold I is mixed with imperial rivalry in central Europe.

eventos.titulo: Leopold and Sobieski agree to help each other
eventos.descripcion: With papal mediation, Leopold I and John III Sobieski agree a defensive alliance. If Vienna or Krakow are attacked, the other sovereign must come to the aid of the ally.

The great vizier Kara Mustafa leads the Ottoman army to Vienna. Leopold leaves the capital and Ernst Rüdiger von Starhemberg organizes the defense as the fortifications suffer weeks of siege and mine work.

eventos.titulo: Poles, Emperors and German Princes gather
eventos.descripcion: Charles V of Lorraine coordinated the imperial forces and joined contingents from Bavaria, Saxony and other territories of the Empire. Sobieski arrives with the Polish army and takes command of the rescue operation.

eventos.titulo: From saving Vienna to moving on to the offensive
eventos.descripcion: After the victory, a new Holy League is formed. The Habsburgs, Poland and Venice transform an emergency defense into a prolonged war against the Ottoman Empire.
The conquest of Buddha shows that Vienna was not an isolated episode. The war that began in 1683 became a Habsburg expansion by Hungary and permanently altered the balance of central Europe.

name: Ireland
summary: The island has a distinct political history: Gaelic kingdoms and lordships, Anglo-Norman families, Crown-titled nobility and powers arising during the wars of the 17th century. The O'Briens, MacCarthy, O'Neill and O'Donnell coexisted and competed with Burgh, Fitzgerald and Butler. English titles alone do not amount to effective control over the population and territory.
notes: The sign distinguishes the supremacy of the high medieval king of the kingdom established in 1542. None of these titles implies effective control of the entire island by itself. Gaelic kingdoms and lordships have their own chips and filters.

He expanded the power of Connacht and disputed Irish supremacy over other regional dynasties. His sons Ruaidrí and Cathal represent two successive responses to the political change of the 12th century.

High King at the beginning of the Anglo-Norman intervention, he tried to preserve his primacy through alliances and negotiation. The Treaty of Windsor of 1175 did not create effective dominion over all of Ireland for any of its signatories; the advance of the conquistadors and family disputes limited their power.

He disputed Connacht with other members of his house and combined Irish alliances with Anglo-Norman agreements. His reign shows the continuity of the Gaelic kingdoms after 1169 and the need to negotiate with the new lordly monarchy.

After being driven from Leinster, he sought support across the sea to regain his kingdom. The arrival of its Anglo-Norman allies in 1169 transformed a struggle between Irish dynasties into a conquest of lasting consequences.

Daughter of Diarmait Mac Murchada, her marriage to Richard de Clare was part of the agreement that attracted Anglo-Norman aid to Leinster. The rights passed down by her daughter Elizabeth connected this Irish heritage with the Marshals and the British aristocracy.

He intervened in Ireland as an ally of Diarmait Mac Murchada and married Aoife. His lordship in Leinster was born of the conquest and of that family agreement; it should not be confused with an automatic and undisputed transmission of Gaelic royalty.

personas.nombre: Isabel de Clare, Countess of Pembroke
personas.resumen: Heiress of Aoife and Strongbow, she passed on an extensive network of lands and rights to her offspring with William Marshal. Her career allowed her to follow the Leinster heritage from an Irish dynasty to the houses of England, Wales and Scotland.

A warrior and servant of several Plantagenet kings, he was also lord of Irish lands by marriage to Elizabeth of Clare. At the end of his life he led the government during the minority of Henry III, linking Leinster's policy to the survival of the English monarchy.

Daughter of William Marshal and Elizabeth of Clare. Her marriage to Gilbert of Clare linked the family's inheritance to the house which, through her daughter Elizabeth, would connect with the Bruce of Scotland.

Chief of the O'Neills who accepted the title of Earl of Tyrone in 1542. The agreement with Henry VIII did not eliminate Gaelic succession or family disputes: both systems legitimized different candidates.

Recognized by Conn Bacach as the county's son and heir, he was rejected by Shane O'Neill and murdered by his supporters. His paternity was discussed: the recognized link is preserved, pointing to that uncertainty.

He defended his election as chief of the O’Neill against the successor system of County Tyrone. He alternated war and negotiation with Elizabeth I, and disputed the predominance of Northern Ireland over other Gaelic houses.

He combined the English title of count with the Gaelic leadership of the O’Neill. He led the coalition of the Nine Years' War, sought Spanish support and ended up in exile after the Flight of the Counts of 1607.
He ruled the lordship of the O'Donnell before ceding leadership to Red Hugh. His family and his wife Iníon Dubh articulated alliances between the northwest Irish and the Gaelic networks of Scotland.

Scottish Gaelic noble and mother of Red Hugh and Rory O'Donnell. She was involved in her family's succession struggle and mobilized support for her children, showing the political role of women in the Irish Sea alliances.

Allied with Hugh O'Neill in the Nine Years' War, he led the O'Donnell from 1592. After the defeat of Kinsale he travelled to Spain to request a new intervention and died in Valladolid, before he could return.

He succeeded Red Hugh and accepted the title of Earl of Tyrconnell after the war. In 1607 he went into exile with Hugh O'Neill: the disappearance of these leaders facilitated a new phase of colonization and confiscations in Ulster.

The son of Cathal Crobderg, he defended his position in Connacht by negotiating and fighting both other Gaelic candidates and the Anglo-Normans. Its rule shows the survival of a regional monarchy after the conquest begun in the 12th century.

He succeeded his father Fedlimid and fought the expansion of the Burghs in Connacht. His victory at Ath an Chip in 1270 temporarily slowed his advance. Disputes between branches of his own family continued after his death.

King of Leinster of the Kavanagh branch, he held the recovery of the power of his lineage against the Anglo-Norman settlements. His son Art Óg continued that policy and became one of Richard II's main adversaries in Ireland.

He strengthened the power of his house in Leinster and resisted the expeditions of Richard II. His authority rested on local alliances and on control of routes and tributes. Its trajectory allows a Gaelic monarchy active in the middle of the Low Middle Ages to follow.

He ruled Thomond and participated in Irish coalitions opposed to the great magnates. His sons Conor and Murrough inherited different positions: continuity of the Gaelic royalty and incorporation into the titled nobility of the Tudors.

He succeeded his father Tairdelbach Donn in the Gaelic monarchy of Thomond. His brother Murrough replaced him according to local succession tradition, while his son Donogh would eventually inherit the county created by the Tudors.

Last king of Thomond before the surrender and restitution agreement with Henry VIII. He surrendered his Gaelic rights and received titles of the Crown. Their previous royalty and the county, whose succession did not follow exactly the same rules, are distinguished.

Son of Conor and nephew of Murrough, he inherited the county within the agreement with the Tudor monarchy. Opposition from other O’Brien members shows the tension between the English title's birthright and the Gaelic chiefdom's rights.

He ruled the Gaelic kingdom of Desmond during the Anglo-Norman expansion in southern Ireland. The continuity of the MacCarthy after his death allows for a distinction between this royality and the Desmond County that the Fitzgeralds would later receive.

Chief of the MacCarthy Mor, he accepted the title of Count of Clancare within Tudor politics. His daughter Ellen inherited a central position in the family domain dispute. The Gaelic royalty, the chiefdom and the county are not presented as equivalent charges.

Daughter and heiress of Donal MacCarthy Mór, her marriage to Florence MacCarthy united rival claims over family domains. Her heritage placed her at the center of the struggle between the Gaelic branches and the Crown administration.

Her marriage to Ellen made her a central figure in the MacCarthy Mores' succession. She negotiated with the Crown and with the Gaelic leaders during the Nine Years' War. She spent much of her later life imprisoned in England.

personas.nombre: Walter de Burgh, conde de Ulster
personas.resumen: He combined the family domains of Connacht with the county of Ulster. His expansion put him in the face of Gaelic powers and made him one of Ireland's great magnates. His son Richard inherited this extensive territorial position.

personas.nombre: Richard de Burgh, conde de Ulster
personas.resumen: Known as the Red Count, he dominated a vast network of Irish lordships. His daughter Elizabeth's marriage to Robert Bruce linked him to the Scottish monarchy, while Edward Bruce's invasion tested his alliances and authority.

He cemented the Fitzgeralds' position in the government of Ireland during the English Dynastic Wars. His family combined service to the Crown, alliances with Gaelic lineages and territorial dominance. Her son Gerald brought that influence to its height.

personas.nombre: Gerald FitzGerald, VIII conde de Kildare
personas.resumen: As a magnate and representative of the Crown, he made his family a central part of the Irish government. His victory at Knockdoe strengthened his ascent over Gaelic and Anglo-Irish rivals. He alternated conflicts and reconciliations with the Tudors.

personas.nombre: Gerald FitzGerald, IX conde de Kildare
personas.resumen: He inherited his father's influence and repeatedly exercised the delegate government of Ireland. Henry VIII's distrust of his power ended in his arrest. His son Thomas' rebellion precipitated the collapse of the family position.

personas.nombre: Thomas FitzGerald, X conde de Kildare
personas.resumen: He led the rebellion of 1534 after receiving news of his father's fate. His defeat and execution in London ended the immediate hegemony of the Kildare. The later restoration of his half-brother preserved the continuity of the lineage.

personas.nombre: Gerald FitzGerald, XI conde de Kildare
personas.resumen: He survived the fall of his family by protecting relatives and allies in Ireland and the continent. He regained the title under Mary Tudor, although the Fitzgeralds no longer enjoyed the old political autonomy.

He led the southern branch of the Fitzgeralds during the Tudor consolidation. Their alliances and conflicts with the Butlers conditioned Munster's policy. His son Gerald inherited a number of domains that would become the center of Desmond's rebellions.

His confrontation with the expansion of Tudor power led to the Desmond rebellions. The defeat, his death and subsequent confiscations transformed Munster. Fitzgerald County is distinct from the former MacCarthy kingdom.

Daughter of James of Desmond, she linked the Fitzgeralds to the Butlers by marriage to James of Ormond. After being widowed, she finally married Gerald of Desmond. Her family alliances crossed the political rivalry between the two houses.

personas.nombre: James Butler, IX Earl of Ormond
personas.resumen: He headed the Butlers during the Tudor administrative expansion. His marriage to Joan FitzGerald linked two of Ireland's great rival houses. His son Thomas would become one of Elizabeth I's main supporters in Munster.

personas.nombre: Thomas Butler, X Earl of Ormond
personas.resumen: Close to Elizabeth I, he held the Butler position and fought the Desmond rebellions. The combination of service to the Crown and family power made him a central player in Munster. His inheritance caused new disputes between his descendants and relatives.

personas.nombre: Walter Butler, XI Earl of Ormond
personas.resumen: He succeeded his uncle Thomas in the title, but he litigated over properties largely attributed to another branch of the family. The marriage of his grandson James to Elizabeth Preston helped to reconcile that divided estate.
Son of Walter Butler and father of the future Duke of Ormond. He died in a shipwreck before he inherited the county, so the succession passed directly from his father to his son James.

He led the royalist cause in Ireland during the Wars of the Three Kingdoms and negotiated with the Catholic Confederation. After the Restoration he again exercised the island's delegate government. Their successive dignitaries of count, marquis and duke differ.

The only surviving daughter of Thomas, X Earl of Ormond, received a significant share of the family estate. Her marriage to Richard Preston and the inheritance of her daughter Elizabeth altered the balance between title and estate within the Butlers.

Heiress to a share of Ormond's estate, her marriage to James Butler brought together conflicting family interests. During the wars, exile and the Restoration intervened in the protection and recovery of the property of her house.

He ran a maritime and territorial network on the west coast of Ireland. He negotiated and fought with Tudor authorities and local rivals; his encounter with Elizabeth I was part of that defense of his interests. His authority was not the equivalent of a crown over Ireland.

Chief of the Mac William Iochtar and second husband of Grace O'Malley. Their alliance combined land and sea power in western Ireland. He was the father of Tibbot, who adapted the family position to the Crown's title system.

The son of Grace O'Malley and Richard Bourke, he maintained family influence through agreements with the Crown. It received the Viscountcy of Mayo in the 17th century. His career shows the transformation of the Gaelic chiefdoms into titled nobility.

Brother of Hugh O'Neill and father of Owen Roe, he links the generation of the Nine Years' War with that of the Irish Confederation. His family maintained military and marriage connections between Ulster and the mainland.

After a long career in the Spanish armies, he returned to Ireland to lead the forces of the Confederate Ulster. His victory at Benburb strengthened his prestige, but political divisions limited cooperation with other Catholic and royalist leaders.

He took part in the rebellion of 1641 and in the initial organization of his forces in Ulster. Owen Roe's arrival changed the military leadership. After the parliamentary conquest he was tried and executed, closing the Confederate resistance.

A veteran of the Spanish armies, he returned to Ireland to command the Confederate army at Leinster. His differences with Owen Roe reflect political and military tensions within the Confederacy. He ended up in exile after the parliamentary advance.

He promoted the recovery of positions for Irish Catholics under James II and reorganized the army. He maintained the Jacobite cause during the war against William of Orange. His county was a new creation, different from the previous title of the O’Donnell.

He distinguished himself in the Jacobite defense during the Irish War and participated in the negotiations that culminated in the Treaty of Limerick. He later joined the French service and died of wounds received at Landen. His county belonged to the nobility created by James II in exile.

He belonged to the branch of the Burkes settled in Connacht. His sons maintained links to the Jacobite cause; his daughter Honora's marriage to Sarsfield linked the lineage to the Irish military exile.

Daughter of the Earl of Clanricarde, she married Patrick Sarsfield and shared the Jacobite exile. After widowing, she married the Duke of Berwick. Her alliances connect Irish families with the exiled court in France.

personas.nombre: James FitzGerald, XI conde de Desmond
personas.resumen: His rivalry with the Butlers over the predominance of Munster motivated attempts at marriage rapprochement between the two houses. His daughter Joan linked Desmond's estate to Ormond's, retaining a strong influence among these lineages.
Last sovereign Stuart, Queen of England, Scotland and Ireland since 1702. Under her reign the Union of 1707 was approved, which created the kingdom of Great Britain; none of her sons survived her.

eventos.descripcion: Royal supremacy over the Church of England turns a marital and political crisis into an ecclesiastical breakdown with lasting consequences.
After the confessional turns of Henry VIII, Edward VI and Mary I, Elizabeth I consolidated a separate Church of England from Rome with a Protestant identity of her own.

people.TIBBOTBOURKE: The son of Grace O'Malley and Richard Bourke, he maintained family influence through agreements with the Crown. It received the Viscountcy of Mayo in the 17th century. His career shows the transformation of the Gaelic chiefdoms into titled nobility.
people.ARTONEILL: Brother of Hugh O'Neill and father of Owen Roe, he links the generation of the Nine Years' War with that of the Irish Confederation. His family maintained military and marriage connections between Ulster and the mainland.
people.OWENROEONEILL: After a long career in the Spanish armies, he returned to Ireland to lead the forces of the Confederate Ulster. His victory at Benburb strengthened his prestige, but political divisions limited cooperation with other Catholic and royalist leaders.
people.PHELIMONEILL: He took part in the rebellion of 1641 and in the initial organization of his forces in Ulster. Owen Roe's arrival changed the military leadership. After the parliamentary conquest he was tried and executed, closing the Confederate resistance.
people.THOMASPRESTON: A veteran of the Spanish armies, he returned to Ireland to command the Confederate army at Leinster. His differences with Owen Roe reflect political and military tensions within the Confederacy. He ended up in exile after the parliamentary advance.
people.RICHARDTALBOT: He promoted the recovery of positions for Irish Catholics under James II and reorganized the army. He maintained the Jacobite cause during the war against William of Orange. His county was a new creation, different from the previous title of the O’Donnell.
people.PATRICKSARSFIELD: He distinguished himself in the Jacobite defense during the Irish War and participated in the negotiations that culminated in the Treaty of Limerick. He later joined the French service and died of wounds received at Landen. His county belonged to the nobility created by James II in exile.
people.WILLIAM7CLANRICARDE: He belonged to the branch of the Burkes settled in Connacht. His sons maintained links to the Jacobite cause; his daughter Honora's marriage to Sarsfield linked the lineage to the Irish military exile.
people.HONORABURKE: Daughter of the Earl of Clanricarde, she married Patrick Sarsfield and shared the Jacobite exile. After widowing, she married the Duke of Berwick. Her alliances connect Irish families with the exiled court in France.
people.JAMES11DESMOND: His rivalry with the Butlers over the predominance of Munster motivated attempts at marriage rapprochement between the two houses. His daughter Joan linked Desmond's estate to Ormond's, retaining a strong influence among these lineages.
people.ANNEQUEEN: Last sovereign Stuart, Queen of England, Scotland and Ireland since 1702. Under her reign the Union of 1707 was approved, which created the kingdom of Great Britain; none of her sons survived her.

name: Tyrol
summary: The county of Tyrol controlled important alpine passes and retained its territorial identity despite being ruled by the Habsburg archduke. Sigismund ceded it to Maximilian I in 1490, while Ferdinand I received it from Charles V in 1522. After the partition of 1564 it formed a separate branch until its meeting with the main line in 1665.

eventos.titulo: Mary of Burgundy is married to Maximilian
eventos.descripcion: The marriage links the Burgundian heritage with the Habsburgs and changes the political balance of Western Europe.
The agreement returned Artois and the Frankish County to the heritage of Mary of Burgundy, while the duchy of Burgundy remained in French hands.
Charles V demands that Luther withdraw. The refusal of the reformer and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transformed a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
Imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Mutinous imperial troops plunder Rome during the Italian Wars.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by simple imperial imposition.
Charles V progressively divided his dominions between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgs.
The Worms Diet promotes common mechanisms of justice, public peace and political organization that seek to make a governmentable empire made up of hundreds of territorial powers.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected King of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I makes the imperial election a European competition. Charles brings together the imperial crown with a dynastic heritage that stretches from the Netherlands to Spain and America.
In the absence of a male heir, Charles VI attempts to secure the indivisibility of the Habsburg dominions and the succession of his future daughter Maria Teresa.

eventos.titulo: Charles VII breaks the Habsburg continuity
eventos.descripcion: In the midst of the War of Austrian Succession, the elector Wittelsbach Carlos Alberto obtains the imperial crown and proves that dignity remains elective, even after centuries of Habsburg predominance.

eventos.titulo: Francis I inaugurated the House of Habsburg-Lorraine
eventos.descripcion: The election of Francis Esteban returns the crown to the dynastic environment of Maria Theresa and creates the Habsburg-Lorraine line.
Joseph II succeeded his father as emperor and, after 1780, attempted to reform the Habsburg dominions quickly, clashing repeatedly with territorial and corporate privileges.
The French revolution upset the European political balance and turned the fate of Maria Antonieta, sister of Joseph II and Leopold II, into an international dynastic problem.

eventos.titulo: Francis II in the face of revolutionary Europe
eventos.descripcion: Francis II inherits the imperial crown in the midst of a revolutionary war. By 1800, the old empire was still in existence, but it was facing a transformation that would culminate a few years later.
Philip Melanchthon presents before Charles V a systematic exhibition of the Lutheran faith, supported by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeated the League of Esmalkalde and captured its two great leaders, but the military victory failed to restore the religious unity of the Empire.

The relief army led by John III Sobieski, with Polish, Habsburg and Holy Empire forces, broke through the Ottoman siege of Vienna on September 12, 1683. The victory opens a new phase of the war in Hungary and reinforces the rise of the Habsburg monarchy in Central Europe.

eventos.titulo: Hungarian rebellion opens a door to the sultan
eventos.descripcion: Imre Thököly leads a Hungarian opposition to the Habsburgs and seeks Ottoman support. The internal conflict of the monarchy of Leopold I is mixed with imperial rivalry in central Europe.

eventos.titulo: Leopold and Sobieski agree to help each other
eventos.descripcion: With papal mediation, Leopold I and John III Sobieski agree a defensive alliance. If Vienna or Krakow are attacked, the other sovereign must come to the aid of the ally.

The great vizier Kara Mustafa leads the Ottoman army to Vienna. Leopold leaves the capital and Ernst Rüdiger von Starhemberg organizes the defense as the fortifications suffer weeks of siege and mine work.

eventos.titulo: Poles, Emperors and German Princes gather
eventos.descripcion: Charles V of Lorraine coordinated the imperial forces and joined contingents from Bavaria, Saxony and other territories of the Empire. Sobieski arrives with the Polish army and takes command of the rescue operation.

eventos.titulo: From saving Vienna to moving on to the offensive
eventos.descripcion: After the victory, a new Holy League is formed. The Habsburgs, Poland and Venice transform an emergency defense into a prolonged war against the Ottoman Empire.
The conquest of Buddha shows that Vienna was not an isolated episode. The war that began in 1683 became a Habsburg expansion by Hungary and permanently altered the balance of central Europe.

eventos.descripcion: John II of France handed over the duchy of Burgundy to his son Philip, origin of the Valois-Borgonian branch.

eventos.titulo: Marriage of Philip and Margaret of Flanders
eventos.descripcion: The marriage to Margaret of Flanders prepared the union of Burgundy with rich Flemish and Burgundy territories.
Juan Sin Miedo is murdered in Montereau. Philip the Good inherits Burgundy and approaches the English side.
Juana is captured by Burgundian forces near Compiègne and ends up in English hands; she is executed at Rouen in 1431.

eventos.titulo: Foundation of the Order of the Golden Toad
eventos.descripcion: Philip the Good founded the Order of the Golden Fleece in the context of his marriage to Isabella of Portugal.
Philip the Good reconciled with Charles VII and broke his alliance with England.
Charles the Temerary succeeded Philip the Good and tried to consolidate a Burgundian territorial block between France and the Empire.

eventos.titulo: Battle of Nancy and death of Charles the Bold
eventos.descripcion: Carlos dies without male heir. His daughter Mary receives an inheritance immediately disputed by Louis XI of France.

eventos.titulo: Mary of Burgundy is married to Maximilian
eventos.descripcion: The marriage links the Burgundian heritage with the Habsburgs and changes the political balance of Western Europe.
The agreement returned Artois and the Frankish County to the heritage of Mary of Burgundy, while the duchy of Burgundy remained in French hands.
Charles V demands that Luther withdraw. The refusal of the reformer and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transformed a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
Imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Mutinous imperial troops plunder Rome during the Italian Wars.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by simple imperial imposition.
Charles V progressively divided his dominions between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgs.
Philip II's naval expedition against England failed after fighting, logistical problems and adverse weather.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected King of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I makes the imperial election a European competition. Charles brings together the imperial crown with a dynastic heritage that stretches from the Netherlands to Spain and America.
Philip Melanchthon presents before Charles V a systematic exhibition of the Lutheran faith, supported by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeated the League of Esmalkalde and captured its two great leaders, but the military victory failed to restore the religious unity of the Empire.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Henry of Navarre a presumed heir. Henry of Guisa reorganizes the Catholic League, backed by Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V achieves an agreement between the Spanish Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States. Philip II contributes an essential part of the resources and his half-brother Don John of Austria receives the supreme command of the Allied fleet.

eventos.titulo: Marriage of Isabella of Castile and Fernando of Aragon
eventos.descripcion: The marriage union binds the two main crowns of the Iberian Peninsula without merging them legally into a single kingdom.
The capitulation of Granada to Elizabeth I and Ferdinand II put an end to the Nasser Emirate; Muhammad XII, Boabdil, surrendered the city.
Charles V demands that Luther withdraw. The refusal of the reformer and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transformed a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
Imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Mutinous imperial troops plunder Rome during the Italian Wars.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by simple imperial imposition.
Charles V progressively divided his dominions between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgs.
Philip II's naval expedition against England failed after fighting, logistical problems and adverse weather.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected King of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I makes the imperial election a European competition. Charles brings together the imperial crown with a dynastic heritage that stretches from the Netherlands to Spain and America.
Philip Melanchthon presents before Charles V a systematic exhibition of the Lutheran faith, supported by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeated the League of Esmalkalde and captured its two great leaders, but the military victory failed to restore the religious unity of the Empire.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Henry of Navarre a presumed heir. Henry of Guisa reorganizes the Catholic League, backed by Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.
After years of war, the Sicilians support Frederick, son of Peter III and Constance of Hohenstaufen. The island develops its own political line in front of the Angevine Naples.

Alfonso V of Aragon defeated the Angevine resistance and entered Naples. For the first time since the Vespera, a single monarch controls Aragon, Trinacria and the continental kingdom, although the crowns retain separate identities.

eventos.titulo: Alfonso's legacy is split up again.
eventos.descripcion: At the death of Alfonso V, Aragon and Trinacria passed to his brother John II, while Naples remained for his son Ferdinand. Personal union does not become a stable merger of crowns.
Louis XII and Ferdinand the Catholic agree to divide the kingdom of Frederick I. Cooperation is short-lived: disputes over the boundaries of partition turn former allies into enemies.

eventos.titulo: Cerignola: The Great Captain Changes the War
eventos.descripcion: Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba's forces defeated the French at Cerignola. The combined use of infantry, field fortifications and firearms consolidated Aragonese position in southern Italy.
A second major victory for the Grand Captain forces the French forces to retreat. The balance born of the 1500 cast is definitely broken in Fernando's favor.

eventos.titulo: Fernando brings together Naples and Trinacria under his crown
eventos.descripcion: The French defeat leaves Ferdinand the Catholic as king of Naples besides Trinacria. The two parts of the former Sicilian monarchy once again share sovereignty, although they will continue to be administered as separate kingdoms.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V achieves an agreement between the Spanish Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States. Philip II contributes an essential part of the resources and his half-brother Don John of Austria receives the supreme command of the Allied fleet.

eventos.titulo: The King's resignation does not force the island
eventos.descripcion: Jaime II agreed to abandon his Sicilian claim to Anagni, but the Sicilians refused to return to the Angevine dominion. They elected their brother Federico and forced the House of Barcelona to split over the future of the island.

Maria and Martin arrived in Sicily with Aragonese support to impose themselves on the barons. The queen's hereditary legitimacy was not enough without military ability. The island's government was once again closely linked to the Crown of Aragon.

The medieval fixture ends before turning those branches into a single fictional succession.

persona.resumen: Emperor of the Holy Empire and sovereign of a composite monarchy that extended to the Iberian Peninsula, Italy, the Netherlands and America. From Philip I he inherited the Franco County, Artois, Namur and Luxembourg, as well as other Dutch territories. It later incorporated Frisia, Utrecht, Overijssel, Drente, Groningen and Güeldres in a phased manner, between 1524 and 1543. He retained the ducal dignity of Burgundy, but did not rule the duchy incorporated into France. From 1535 he kept Milan under imperial control; the investiture and subsequent possession of Philip II must be distinguished from that government.

name: Castellbó
summary: The Viscounty of Castellbó was part of the Foix heritage networks on both sides of the Pyrenees. The line of Roger Bernardo, son of Gaston I, allows us to understand the succession after Gaston Febus. Matthew and his sister Isabel came from this collateral branch and inherited Foix and Bearne. Elizabeth's marriage to Archambaud de Grailly passed the estate on to a descendant with another male ancestry. Sharing headlines does not make the Catalan Viscounty, the County of Foix and the County of Bearne equivalent.
